newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields off slightly pre-tender.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields off slightly pre-tender.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained around their opening lower levels ahead of a A$500 million two-tranche T-bond tender, the first of this fiscal year.
Australian bond yields remained around their opening lower levels ahead of a A$500 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender, the first of the 1997/98 fiscal year.
Traders expect the market to find few problems absorbing the tender stock given its relatively small size and due to the recent liquidity tightness after the recent strong rally.
The offering comprises A$200 million of October 2007 bond, the current 10-year benchmark bond, and A$300 million of the September 2009 issue.
The tender result is due at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

The outcome of the tender may provide the market's direction this afternoon, although the main focus remains on monetary policy and next Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting where a 50 basis points easing is expected to be endorsed.
The modest fall in yields was largely a reflection of Monday's rally in U.S. Treasuries, which are expecting a favourable outcome to the second quarter U.S. employment costs index later on Tuesday.
Local data for the June balance of goods and services failed to make much of a stir in the market, despite posting a record A$1.964 billion surplus.

The sharp widening in the surplus from A$787 million in May was due largely to a 23 percent rise in goods exports which included A$1.8 billion of gold reserves sold by the Reserve Bank. Goods imports were up 9.0 percent.

"The imports rise...is starting to look quite interesting in terms of potential for economic growth to revive later on in the year. But near term that won't effect bond market sentiment, because the inflation readings are still exceptionally good," Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
Wednesday sees the release of June building approvals.

The local market underperformed the U.S. ahead of the tender. New Zealand debt partially recovered from their weak start, but were still underperforming the bloc on the day after the market was once again undermined by a weak N.Z. dollar.
